changes.title: A New Pain Treatment for Dogs with Chiari-like Malformation and Syringomyelia

record.description: Chiari-like malformation (CM) and syringomyelia (SM) are common in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels and can cause chronic nerve pain. Affected dogs may scratch at the air near their neck or shoulder ("phantom scratching"), yelp for no clear reason, dislike being touched around the head and neck, or seem restless or less playful. Current medications help some dogs, but many continue to have pain or side effects. The University of Florida Veterinary Hospital is studying a new investigational drug called AZ194. It works by blocking NaV1.7, a channel that nerves use to send pain signals. AZ194 is administered as a nasal spray, and its approach differs from the pain medications currently used for CM/SM. The goal is to find out whether it reduces pain and improves quality of life in affected dogs.
record.tagline: Testing a new nasal spray for Chiari-like malformation and syringomyelia (CM/SM) pain in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels
record.name: A New Pain Treatment for Dogs with Chiari-like Malformation and Syringomyelia
